_comment: PEMF -- core narrative events.
Drop your own .json files in this folder; every one of them is loaded.
RULES (all enforced at load time -- see pemf.log if an event is rejected):
* EASIEST WAY -- write a {placeholder} and supply NO args at all:
{crew} {morale} {gold} {months} {port} {portNation} {portType}
e.g. "body": "Land ho! {port} off the bow!"
The {port...} ones name the port NEAREST the ship when the event
fires, and read blank if none is in range. Write {{ for a literal
brace. Do not mix placeholders with an explicit args list.
* The hard way, if you want it: the engine's own tokens @NUM, @HAPPY,
@CITYNAME, @NATIONALITY, @LOCTYPE with a matching args list.
@CITYNAME COSTS THREE ARGUMENT SLOTS -- it is a three-word name
record, not a string. One "nearestCity" arg supplies all three.
* The number of tokens must EXACTLY match the number of args supplied.
A surplus token reads stack garbage from a 2004 engine.
* args may be: "crew", "morale", "plunder", "months",
"nearestCity", "nearestCityNation", "nearestCityType", or an integer.
* text must be plain 7-bit ASCII -- no smart quotes, no accents.
* effect ops: addPlunder, setPlunder, addCrew, setCrew.
* 1 to 6 options per event.
KINDS:
"kind": "choice"  (default) a modal card that asks the player to decide.
"kind": "notice"  on-screen text while sailing -- the same look as the
game's own 'Press r to return to ship'. Never interrupts, has no
options, and takes "seconds" (1-30, default 4) instead.
NOTICE PLACEMENT -- "anchor", allowed on ANY notice whatever fired it:
"anchor": "screen"  (default) a line at the top of the screen.
"anchor": "ship"    hangs over your vessel IN THE WORLD and FOLLOWS IT
as you sail, drawn by the same routine the game uses to label other
ships, and easing out over its last second. Keep the text short:
it is drawn at world scale and a long line runs off the screen.
TRIGGERS (optional -- without one an event only fires by hand):
{ "type": "elapsedSailing", "seconds": 120, "cooldown": 600 }
fires after that many seconds of ACTUAL SAILING. Time in port, in
menus, or on any other screen does not count toward it.
{ "type": "nearPort", "distance": 3000, "rearm": 6000 }
fires on coming within 'distance' of any port. Re-arms only once
further out than 'rearm', so hugging a coast cannot spam it.
Measured over two sessions: the closest the ship came to a port was
988 once and 1620 another time -- it depends entirely on the route.
~3000 is 'harbour in sight'; ~1000 only fires if you sail right in.
pemf.log reports live distances and 'closestEver' for tuning.
{ "type": "stateCrosses", "field": "morale", "below": 2 }
fires when a live value CROSSES a threshold. 'field' is one of crew,
gold, morale (0 mutinous .. 4 devoted) or months. Give exactly one
of 'below' or 'above'. Edge-triggered like nearPort: it fires on
crossing and cannot fire again until the value crosses back out.
Note 'gold' is UNDIVIDED PLUNDER, not your total wealth.
All three also accept "once": true and "cooldown": <seconds>.
elapsedSailing and nearPort require that you are under way; stateCrosses
only requires that a career is loaded.
A '%' is safe here: the engine formatter is @-token based and never calls
printf, so there is no format-string hazard.

events.body: The bosun corners you below decks, hat in hand and eyes hard. Your crew of {crew} has gone {morale}, and the men have been counting the days since the plunder was last divided.

options.text: Send him back to his post.
options.outcome: You send him back to his post empty handed. The bosun says nothing, but word of it runs the length of the ship before the watch is out.
The rum goes round and the deck turns loud. It costs you @NUM pieces of eight, but your crew of @NUM drinks your health and means it.

options.text: Divide the plunder here and now.
options.outcome: You call the hands aft and split the take where every man can see it counted. Your crew of {crew} goes back to work satisfied, and the hold is emptier for it.

events.body: A hush falls over the deck. Your crew of {crew} stands {morale}, and word spreads that something has changed aboard this ship.

options.text: Say nothing and hold your course.

events.body: The cook reports the salt pork is turning. You have {crew} mouths to feed and {months} months of sailing behind you, and the men have noticed the smell before you did.

options.text: Put the men on short rations.
options.outcome: The ration is cut and nobody thanks you for it. The hands eat in silence and watch the horizon for landfall.

options.text: Throw the spoiled stores overboard and make for port.
options.outcome: The barrels go over the side. It costs you @NUM in stores, but the air below decks is fit to breathe again.
